title: A replacement deadline, year by year

blocks.text: A water utility is lining a failing trunk main. First a temporary bypass pipe goes in (project `BY`), then the permanent replacement (project `RP`). The utility's rule: the replacement starts in the same year as the bypass or at most `within` years later, because the bypass is only rated for that long. A bypass is never laid without its replacement, and a replacement is never started without its bypass.

A colleague wrote the rule in `add_aggregated_deadline` as rows on the two projects' weighted start-year sums. It refuses exactly the right whole-number schedules, but the LP bound of the planning model is loose and its solves are slow.

Write `add_deadline_rows(model, x, bypass, replacement, within)` in `deadline.py`: the same rule, written so that it checks the schedule year by year. Nothing in the lesson writes this rule; derive it from the lesson's idea of running totals ("started by year $`t`$").
The model so far, with $`T_{BY}`$ and $`T_{RP}`$ the years each project may start in, $`Y`$ their union, and $`W`$ the value of `within`:
Write your rows in this notation first, each with its quantifier and a label, then code them. Check them against a bypass started in the last year of its window.

The tests fix a schedule by its variables' bounds and ask the solver whether it is allowed, so any correct set of rows passes; one more test checks that on a small LP your rows give a smaller LP value (a tighter bound: for a maximization the LP value bounds every plan from above) than the colleague's. About ten lines in total.

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass

from ortools.math_opt.python import mathopt


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Project:
    pid: str
    starts: tuple[int, ...]          # the years it may start in


def start_variables(model: mathopt.Model, projects: list[Project], integer: bool = True) -> dict:
    return {(p.pid, t): model.add_variable(lb=0, ub=1, is_integer=integer, name=f"x_{p.pid}_{t}")
            for p in projects for t in p.starts}


def add_aggregated_deadline(model, x, bypass: Project, replacement: Project, within: int) -> None:
    """The colleague's version: equal funding, then two rows on the start years' weighted sums."""
    funded_b = sum(x[bypass.pid, s] for s in bypass.starts)
    funded_r = sum(x[replacement.pid, u] for u in replacement.starts)
    model.add_linear_constraint(funded_r == funded_b)
    year_b = sum(s * x[bypass.pid, s] for s in bypass.starts)
    year_r = sum(u * x[replacement.pid, u] for u in replacement.starts)
    model.add_linear_constraint(year_r >= year_b)
    model.add_linear_constraint(year_r <= year_b + within * funded_b)


def add_deadline_rows(model, x, bypass: Project, replacement: Project, within: int) -> None:
    """The replacement starts in the bypass's start year or up to `within` years later, and only then."""
    years = sorted(set(bypass.starts) | set(replacement.starts))
    for t in years:
        bypass_by_t = sum(x[bypass.pid, s] for s in bypass.starts if s <= t)
        model.add_linear_constraint(
            bypass_by_t <= sum(x[replacement.pid, u] for u in replacement.starts if u <= t + within),
            name=f"deadline_{t}")
        model.add_linear_constraint(
            sum(x[replacement.pid, u] for u in replacement.starts if u <= t) <= bypass_by_t,
            name=f"not_before_{t}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    bypass, replacement = Project("BY", (2027, 2028, 2029)), Project("RP", (2027, 2028, 2029, 2030))
    model = mathopt.Model()
    x = start_variables(model, [bypass, replacement])
    add_deadline_rows(model, x, bypass, replacement, 1)
    print(len(list(model.linear_constraints())), "rows")

cases.says: a replacement inside the deadline is allowed, and one after it is refused
a replacement starting in the deadline year itself is allowed
a replacement one year past the deadline is refused
a bypass with no replacement at all is refused
a replacement before its bypass, or without one, is refused
a bypass started so late that no replacement year is left is refused
on a small LP the year-by-year rows give a lower bound than the colleague's rows

origin.section: A Tighter LP Bound Means a Smaller Search

concepts: forms that allow the same plans can have different LP bounds, and the cumulative one is never weaker
a precedence with a lag can be written as one aggregated row or as one cumulative row per year, and both allow the same whole-number plans
